content:
local notation "a" => 1 in
#check a -- Unknown identifier `«a»`

Why doesn't this work? (The local doesn't change anything, but the sample would be silly without it. Well, it's already silly since in this case you could let +zeta, but imagine the notation is something nontrivial.)
These similar samples are perhaps relevant:

local macro_rules | `(a) => `(1) in
#check a -- 1 : Nat

local macro "a" : term => `(1) in
#check a -- Unknown identifier `«a»`
Well, it parses the body before it elaborates the notation command.
I guess this is a related issue: lean4#181

Oh, I see. So: in each case it parses perfectly fine as an identifier, but the notation and macro commands try to introduce a new way of parsing it that doesn't come into being before the macro-expansion of in occurs, so they can't fire. Whereas the macro_rules example fires on the identifier a so you get to turn the a into 1 when you do more macro expansion in the #check.
(and the french quotes are to disambiguate from the notation which exists at elab time in each case)

So, arguably this is a limitation of the definition of in, because if I understand correctly it could easily be defined in such a way as to make this work? (though it does not seem like a particularly high-value feature)

This is a limitation of parsing: Because in is not a command on its own but a combinator of commands, parsing a x in y command only ends after also parsing the body. So what would need to happen is that the parser would need to half-elaborate the notation command before parsing the #check a command; which is difficult because parsers in Lean are pure.
